Management believes Free Cash Flow, Free Cash Flow Margin and Free Cash Flow Conversion are useful because they allow for an effective evaluation of both our operating and financial performance, as well as the capital intensity of our business, and subsequently the ability of our operations to generate cash flow that is available to distribute to our shareholders, reduce leverage or support acquisition activities. Our computations of these measures may differ from the computations of similarly titled measures of other companies. Normalized Revenue is used by our management and is useful to investors, research analysts and other external users of our Financial Statements to assess our operating performance on a basis that reflects our expected go-forward business following our initial public offering. Because our results for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 include only a partial period of operations as a public company and do not reflect the full effect of certain items that we expect to characterize our operations on a go-forward basis, we present Normalized Revenue to illustrate what our Revenue would approximate had these items been in effect for the full periods presented. We define Normalized Revenue as Revenue adjusted for normalizing adjustments, which consist of the addition of revenue from assets contributed in the corporate reorganization in connection with our initial public offering and the exclusion of revenue attributable to our predecessor that are not expected to recur on a go-forward basis. Normalized Adjusted EBITDA and Normalized Adjusted EBITDA Margin are used by our management and are useful to investors, research analysts and other external users of our Financial Statements to assess our operating performance on a basis that reflects our expected go-forward business following our initial public offering. Net leverage, calculated as net debt divided by the midpoint of the Company’s full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance, was 0.4x. Total liquidity was $142 million, comprised of $12 million of cash and cash equivalents and $130 million of available borrowing capacity under the Company’s revolving credit facility, which includes $200 million of initial capacity and the ability to request up to an additional $100 million. EagleRock funded the Intrepid Ranch acquisition, which was completed for a total purchase price of $78.3 million, primarily through its revolving credit facility. Following the initial draw in August, the Company repaid $10 million in each of September and October, partially offset by approximately $16 million of borrowings in October to fund the Acquisitions. The Company expects to continue allocating approximately $10 million per month toward debt reduction. 2026 Outlook For the full year 2026, the Company is raising its Adjusted EBITDA guidance to a range of $133 million to $137 million, inclusive of the Intrepid Ranch acquisition. The $135 million midpoint compares to a $131 million midpoint in the Company’s prior guidance, with the $4 million increase reflecting approximately $2 million from Intrepid Ranch and approximately $2 million of additional organic growth. two bolt-on acquisitions in the Midland Basin totaling approximately 2,000 acres for $15.4 million in aggregate (the “Acquisitions”). EagleRock funded the acquisitions through a combination of cash on hand and borrowings under its existing revolving credit facility. The Double Eagle V Dedication covers approximately 35,000 acres in Midland and Glasscock Counties and increases the total acreage dedicated to EagleRock by Double Eagle in the Midland Basin by approximately 50%, to approximately 105,000 acres. This agreement further strengthens our longstanding relationship with Double Eagle, one of the most active private operators in the Midland Basin and EagleRock’s largest shareholder. Importantly, the dedication underscores the strength of our capital-light business model, generating additional royalty revenue without requiring any capital investment by EagleRock. While it is early to provide specific financial guidance, we expect robust revenue contribution from this dedication beginning in 2027, with further meaningful growth in subsequent years consistent with Double Eagle’s drilling and completions cadence. The two Midland Basin acquisitions were acquired at a valuation of less than 10x EBITDA, with one acquisition directly adjacent to our existing Shallow Valley footprint and the other directly adjacent to the newly announced Double Eagle V acreage dedication. These strategically located assets expand EagleRock’s water supply, storage, disposal capabilities, and include sand development optionality, creating opportunities to capture incremental operating synergies and unlock additional revenue across the entire Double Eagle dedicated footprint and the broader Midland Basin. Pro forma for the transactions, EagleRock’s Midland Basin footprint is approximately 44,000 acres plus approximately 105,000 dedicated acres. The acquisitions closed concurrent with signing. “The Double Eagle V Dedication builds on a relationship that already anchors our Midland Basin position, and it requires no upfront capital from EagleRock,” said Greg Pipkin, Chief Executive Officer of EagleRock. “The two acquisitions follow the same approach. They sit next to assets we already have, expand our water supply and storage, and are accretive.
